name: Saint Lucia
summary: Saint Lucia's Civil Code lets an adult dispose of property by will and no reserved share was found. The Code also recognises trusts under English principles. Without a will, a spouse takes one third and the children two thirds. The Hague Trusts Convention is not in force.
foreign_law_note: No source read states Saint Lucia's conflict rule for a foreign national's estate.
trust_note: Not in the HCCH status table. Civil Code art. 916A allows trusts of movable or immovable property, with English law on trustees' duties. The International Trust Act, Cap. 12.19 was repealed with effect from 30 June 2021 (Act 16 of 2018). No private foundation statute was found.
open_questions: Only intestacy arts. 567A-568 and art. 770 were read; absence of a reserved share is inferred, not confirmed.
Revised Laws pages are marked 'not yet authenticated through a Commencement Order'.
Whether any foundation law exists was not confirmed.
Private foundations: no source found either way; not finding a foundation law is not evidence that there is none.
